html:
SMTO-EXE-0064 — SMTO lost contact with the Gateway computer during a desktop task

GUID: f99bbbc1-241d-5ac8-b835-c19144569eed
Slug: desktop-gateway-lost
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: desktop

What happened

  • SMTO asked another computer to work with its apps or windows, but got no usable answer from the Gateway, the helper program SMTO uses on that computer. SMTO uses this message when it was only looking or hadn't started a change.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, find the Gateway for that computer, and select Check connection. This shows whether SMTO can reach that Gateway right now and what went wrong last time.
  2. If the check fails, make sure that computer is switched on, awake, signed in, connected to the network, and that the Gateway program is running. SMTO sends desktop requests only to that one computer and never switches to another, so it has to be on and reachable.
  3. When Check connection succeeds, make sure someone is signed in to that computer's desktop, then ask SMTO in the conversation to continue. The Gateway can only work with apps and windows while a desktop session is open on that computer.

What success looks like

  • Check connection succeeds for that Gateway, and SMTO's next desktop request returns a result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer. If you had stopped the task, look at that computer's screen before asking SMTO to open, close or quit anything again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Server's Desktop request (or its cancel call) to the selected Gateway failed at the HTTP or outbound-session level for a read or a proven pre-dispatch failure, so no usable desktop result came back.

What this means

  • The Desktop route received a Gateway HTTP/transport error or its cancellation call failed. Read and proven pre-dispatch failures retain this category, while uncertain mutations use reconciliation. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • The Desktop route received a Gateway HTTP/transport error or its cancellation call failed. Read and proven pre-dispatch failures retain this category, while uncertain mutations use reconciliation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect retained status, failure phase and whether the call was a read, mutation or cancellation; keep the original Gateway identity.

How to fix it

  • Check the selected Gateway's reachability (Settings › Setup › Gateways › Check connection, and the Gateway log for /desktop/operation or /desktop/cancel) and that it advertises the needed desktop_windows, desktop_applications or desktop_processes tags rather than desktop_unavailable. Reconnect the same Gateway and refresh its capabilities before observing again; if the cancel call failed, observe processes and windows to settle the original operation before any new one.
  • Restore the selected Gateway route and inspect any original operation before new desktop work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Reconnect the same selected Gateway and refresh its capabilities before observing again.

How to verify the fix

  • The same verified route is restored and the original desktop operation is settled before a new action.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass identity protection or automatically replay an uncertain mutation.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
